messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
a faint new vibration appears under load while you are handling A belt-driven feeder beside a noisy machine. You have only a few minutes before someone else needs it. How do you approach it?

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R025", "response": "i hold the feeder steady with one hand and my grip clicks. the vibration clicks too. i move it two centimeters away, then put it down. “i did not,” i say. “i was holding it. i was younger.”"}, {"id": "R026", "response": "i pull my hand back from the feeder before the vibration catches. i put my palm on the belt-driven housing and mark the faint vibration with pencil. i wait for the machine to move, then mark the feeder’s position."}, {"id": "R027", "response": "i tap the belt. i listen. i leave the feeder by the machine. i put the wrench down and turn the feeder. the vibration comes back. i leave it. i will keep it."}, {"id": "R028", "response": "i put the feeder on the wall and put the vibration under it. the wall stays open because the belt pulls it. i move the feeder back and put the vibration beside it. the light stays on, so i put the feeder back on the wall."}, {"id": "R029", "response": "I keep the belt beside the feeder and run one short cycle. I touch the worn teeth with grease, then leave the feeder alone for one minute. I keep the vibration for one short run, leave the belt beside the machine, and mark the worn teeth with grease before anyone else tries it."}, {"id": "R030", "response": "I turn the vibration once between finger and thumb. “It is there,” I say. The machine stops. I leave the feeder beside it and put the plate over the door. I leave the noise alone."}, {"id": "R031", "response": "i put the feeder under the machine and watch the vibration. i put the belt in my palm, then turn it back over. i put the feeder in the machine and pocket the vibration as proof. the machine is still moving, so i will leave the feeder there. maybe the vibration is waiting for someone."}, {"id": "R032", "response": "i tap the belt and listen for the vibration, then leave the feeder alone and check the motor. i say sorry to the machine, then leave it alone. i check the load, then write the new one under the old one."}, {"id": "R033", "response": "i touch the vibration. i look at the machine. i put my palm under the gate. the gate stays cold. i move the belt. the fence stays quiet. i put the gate lid on the board. the vibration stays."}, {"id": "R034", "response": "i rub my palm and look at the vibration. i move the feeder away from it, then test the belt under load. if the vibration stays, i stop and let the machine take it. i do not call the noise a fault just because the bench is busy."}, {"id": "R035", "response": "i photograph the vibration and check the pulley before touching it. my hand knocks the belt-driven feeder off. sorry—sorry, i’m checking the pulley anyway. the machine continues to make the noise. i move it away and leave the photo behind."}, {"id": "R036", "response": "i put the feeder on the bench and mark the place where the vibration came. then i move the feeder closer to the machine. the vibration goes. i put the mark back on the bench. the machine waits. i do not say what it did."}]
